Sephiroth returns in Final Fantasy Resonance as a Vision you can equip to your party members. He is available in mid-late game and is one of the best Vision you can get. He is also a pretty tough boss fight that will need preparation if you want to win. This guide goes over exactly how to find Sephiroth in Final Fantasy Resonance , and every detail you'll need to beat him.
How to Find Sephiroth in Final Fantasy Resonance
Like most of the Visions, Sephiroth is in a sanctum with a Vision crystal. His is a little different because it is hidden on the map and unavailable until Chapter 5 , when you can freely use your airship.
Once you can soar through the skies, travel over the waters of the Kingdom of Grandshelt. You'll find Whirlpool Hollow, the whirlpool between the two northern land masses of Grandshelt. It is just north-east of the Village of Kol.
You cannot land, so just hover over the whirlpool and "Whirlpool Hollow" will show up for you to enter directly from the airship. When you get in, it looks like any other Vision sanctum. When you go to the crystal, however, you will be asked if you want to challenge Sephiroth after the initial dialogue.
Sephiroth is a tough boss fight, especially if you attempt it as early as possible. Don't be fooled by the fact that he's level 45; you'll want to be much higher than that to make the fight easier.
There are a few things you can do to make this fight more manageable:
Rain built as a tank with the Multi-Cover ability from the WoL Vision.
Lid with the Mechamog Scan ability unlocked .
The Sephiroth Vision boss fight has three phases. Each phase happens when his health hits a certain threshold. Sephiroth has 250k HP and no elemental weakness in the beginning.
This is the main reason the fight can be difficult at lower levels, and it provides the biggest barrier to initially overcome.
In the first phase, Sephiroth has extremely high magic defense and will use Masamune in Waiting on the first turn. This parries and counters all physical attacks, making them useless. You will need to use only elemental attacks during this, but they deal low damage because of his defenses.
If you hit Sephiroth with an elemental weakness, it will pressure him. This makes him use more powerful attacks, but will be easier to stagger. Normally, you would not be able to do this in phase one, but Lid has the key to making this fight easier.
Lid's Mechamog Scan ability will add a random elemental weakness to Sephiroth . This immensely helps in phase one and makes getting to phase two much easier and quicker. The best part is that this weakness stays for the entire boss fight , even when he switches phases and elemental resistances.
Whether you use Lid's ability or not, you'll just need to keep using magic attacks until you get his health down to 200K. When this happens, he will use One-Winged Angel on his next action to start the next phase.
If you get him down to 200K HP, and still have action before Sephiroth's turn, he will be immune to all damage until he uses One-Winged Angel.
During this phase, Sephiroth will periodically use an attack that leaves every party member at 1 HP. He will then enhance himself with one element and gain elemental resistance to all but one. Sephiroth absorbs whatever element he enhances.
If you use Mechamog Skin, he will keep that weakness. If it is the element he enhances, it will stay a weakness and not be absorbed.
You will need to use Libra every time he switches elements if you want to see the new weakness, or just keep using the random weakness you give him with Lid.
He will no longer parry and counter physical attacks, so you can use anything you want in this phase. Once he reaches 50k HP, he will cast Divine Proclamation on his next action to start the third, and final, phase.
The final phase is a race against the Divine Proclamation timer. You will need to defeat him before the countdown on his buff bar hits 0, or you lose. When it reaches 0, he uses Divine Proclamation to instantly kill every party member and end the fight.
During this phase, Sephiroth absorbs all Dark elemental attacks , and is weak to Light elemental attacks, plus whatever weakness you give him.
He will switch between powerful magic and physical attacks, so be prepared. You'll need to go all-out in this phase to defeat him before the timer is up.
Rain can be used to soak up nearly all the damage while Lid and another attacker focus on dealing damage to Sephiroth.
If you've unlocked Rain's "Power Within" buff, use that first.
Fina is the best healer and is used mostly to keep Rain alive and cure status effects. During phase 3, Fina's Holy ability can deal a lot of damage, which can help beat the damage check before Divine Proclamation wipes the party.
Lid's Mechamog Scan can be used multiple times if needed. If you don't get a favorable element, just use it again, and it will replace Sephiroth's weakness with another one. Besides that, Lid will be used to deal damage. It is best if you can use her Mechabo abilities, since they can additionally debuff Sephiroth to make him easier to beat.
The final member should be a dedicated attacker. Sakura is a great one because of her strong magic attacks. You will absolutely want to level the Terra Vision to 9 to unlock "Break the Limit." This raises the damage cap from 9,999 to 99,999, basically from 10k to 100k. This should be used on your dedicated attacker, Lid, and possibly Fina.
You use Mechamog Scan on the first turn, and if it is a favorable weakness, you're set for the rest of the battle.
Summon an Esper with Fina if it matches the weakness, or if you have Bahamut.
Use Libra during Phase 2 if you want to know the additional weakness.
If you're still struggling, you can always level up some more and try again. You might need to wait until 60+ to beat Sephiroth.
